source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

rural.evidence: Government infrastructure push (housing, roads, railways, gas pipelines) cited as a demand tailwind for TMT bars/long steel volumes; no rural-specific revenue split disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Company commentary attributes long-term volume growth to government-driven infrastructure expansion (railways, roads, gas pipelines, urban housing), but no quantified % of revenue tied to government capex was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports were about 10.6% of turnover per the FY2025-26 BRSR filing (a proxy figure from the following fiscal year; FY24-25-specific export % was not located).

pli_scheme.evidence: Shyam Metalics Flat Products was selected to invest under the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for specialty steel, covering high-strength steel for automotive and CRGO electrical steel.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Long-term debt fell sharply to about ₹6.7 crore in FY25 from roughly ₹300 crore in FY24 (a ~98% reduction), indicating minimal residual debt exposure; no floating-rate % disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company uses forward contracts/hedges against USD, GBP and EUR revenue exposure; mark-to-market hedge losses were referenced in subsequent-period earnings calls (e.g., ~$10M in Q1 FY26 with further ~$14M to be realized), evidencing an active but partial hedging programme rather than full cover.
inr_exposure.evidence: US revenue share was ~33% of FY25 total; EMEA's share was ~38% (dented by weaker GBP/EUR); APAC and India combined share rose to ~29% (this bucket includes domestic India revenue, not export alone).

china_plus_one.evidence: Industry/analyst commentary positions Divi's Labs as a beneficiary of the 'China+1' CDMO diversification trend as Western pharma majors de-risk supply chains; the Custom Synthesis segment saw a meaningful recovery in H2 FY25 after roughly two years of weak API-segment performance, and the company signed a long-term supply agreement with a global pharma major alongside a ₹650-700 crore capacity expansion. No explicit 'China+1' framing quote from the AR itself was located.

crude_exposure.evidence: Solvent (petroleum-derivative) costs rose sharply amid Middle East-driven crude volatility; the company shifted to a 3-month rolling inventory strategy and relies on backward integration and solvent recovery to reduce exposure to single-source, petroleum-linked inputs. No exact % of raw materials tied to crude derivatives was disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: About 88% of FY25 revenue was derived from exports (Europe 56.46%, North America 16.18%, Asia 11.35%, RoW 3.99%), implying substantial USD/EUR-denominated revenue; specific hedging policy details were not found in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: No confirmation found that Divi's Laboratories is a beneficiary of the Bulk Drugs PLI scheme; the scheme primarily targets new/incremental capacity for 53 critical KSMs/APIs with high import dependence.

rural.evidence: Company has expanded beyond metros into tier-2 cities (Lucknow, Patna, Ranchi, Indore), with management stating quality care drives strong financial returns across Tier-2 markets and demand for premium care exists outside traditional urban hubs; no rural revenue % disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Debt-to-equity ratio reported to have fallen from 46.6% to 15.8% over five years with debt well covered by operating cash flow (113.2%), indicating low leverage, but no floating-rate liability split disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Revenue from international patients was approximately 6% of total revenue in FY2024-25 (up 8% YoY to INR 2,086 million); this is foreign-patient revenue rather than conventional export/USD invoicing, and no hedging policy was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company is expanding export capacity via its Dubai facility (utilisation 80-85%) targeting Middle East and Africa as a growth avenue, part of a broader capacity build (5MT to 7-10MT by FY28-30); no explicit China+1/supply-chain-diversification framing was found attributing this to customers replacing Chinese sourcing.

govt_capex.evidence: Management commentary cites policy tailwinds including PMAY (Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, extended to Dec-25, 94 lakh homes delivered) and repo-rate cuts supporting housing demand; affordable/mid-segment housing (below Rs 1 crore) is over 50% of housing sales and housing/residential demand is described as a major driver, but no single revenue % tied specifically to government capex/infra spending was disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw materials are HR coil, galvanized coil and zinc (steel-linked, not crude-oil-linked); HRC prices are market-linked and a source of margin volatility. Company sources over 80% of HR coil from Tata Steel and JSW Steel. Not a crude-oil exposure.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports were approximately 6% of sales as of Q4FY25 per broker result-update commentary; company is expanding export capacity (Dubai plant) targeting Middle East/Africa. No hedging policy disclosure found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Search results reference the structural-steel-tubes sector broadly benefiting from PLI-scheme-supported growth, but no confirmation was found that APL Apollo itself is a direct PLI scheme beneficiary or discloses PLI-linked revenue.

china_plus_one.evidence: Industry commentary (third-party, e.g. The Ken) discusses a broader pharma-sector China+1 API trend, but Glenmark's own recent strategic action was divesting a 75% stake in its API subsidiary Glenmark Life Sciences to Nirma (reducing its holding from 82.84% to 7.84%), explicitly framed by the company as "moving up the value chain" toward branded/innovative business rather than deepening API/China+1 diversification.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 consolidated revenue was INR 133,217 million (+12.8% YoY). Europe contributed 21.4% of consolidated revenue in FY25 (grew ~17.6-18%). Quarterly disclosures show North America and India as other major contributors, but a confirmed full-year USD/export revenue percentage and hedging policy were not found in accessible sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Glenmark's API business (the PLI-eligible bulk-drug operation) was housed in subsidiary Glenmark Life Sciences, in which Glenmark divested a 75% stake to Nirma Limited, cutting its holding to 7.84%; a search-cited figure of "INR 25,813 Cr PLI investment" could not be verified as Glenmark-specific (appears to reference industry-wide pharma PLI figures) and is not used.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company describes a "local for local" manufacturing strategy serving 23 domestic market segments (celebrating 75 years of India manufacturing) rather than an export/China+1 diversification narrative; exports are cited at roughly 10% of the revenue mix, with growth in export markets noted specifically within the Distribution Solutions division, but no explicit China+1 framing was found.

govt_capex.evidence: FY2024 revenue growth was driven by the Electrification segment, supported by data center orders, EPC customer execution, and export growth in Distribution Solutions; record orders of Rs 13,079 crore and record revenue of Rs 12,188 crore were reported, but no revenue % was specifically attributed to government (vs. private) capex.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports are approximately 10% of ABB India's revenue mix. Q2 2025 profit fell 20% YoY partly on forex volatility; company disclosure notes profitability was affected by higher material costs, forex, and QCO-related imported material usage, "partly offset through commodity hedging and efficiency gains" — no detailed forex-specific hedging policy (forwards/natural hedge ratio) was found.

pli_scheme.evidence: No source found confirming ABB India as a direct PLI scheme beneficiary; PLI electronics-manufacturing beneficiary lists found in search (Foxconn, Wistron, Pegatron, etc.) do not include ABB India.

china_plus_one.evidence: Communication-cable segment exports (~35-40% of that segment, per Q1 FY26 call) grew to the US and Europe on data-center/AI-driven optic-fiber demand; company revamped its export team to 'explore multiple geographies' and cited exports as 'a key incremental lever.' No explicit China+1 framing found in sources reviewed.

rural.evidence: Company is expanding distribution to ~2,50,000 retailers with a focus on Tier 2/3 cities and rural areas; electrical-cable growth partly attributed to agricultural and solar cable demand, but no rural revenue % disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Analyst commentary (post Budget 2026-27) cites 'real estate, government capex and a data-center-led fiber upcycle' as demand drivers for the Cables & Wires business; no company-disclosed revenue share tied to government capex found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company has historically been near debt-free; FY24 long-term debt was only ~Rs 8 million (vs Rs 3 million in FY23) with finance costs up 63.7% YoY, implying minimal floating-rate liability exposure.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials are copper and PVC compounds (PVC resin cost is crude-derivative linked), but no explicit crude-oil-linked raw-material percentage was disclosed in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Rupee depreciation cited as a margin headwind alongside rising material costs; growing US/Europe fiber-cable exports increase USD exposure, but no specific USD revenue % or hedging policy found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Optical-fiber cable manufacturing falls under DoT's telecom PLI scheme (31 companies deemed eligible industry-wide) and brokers cite 'PLI scheme continuity' as a positive backdrop, but sources reviewed did not confirm Finolex Cables specifically as an approved PLI beneficiary or disclose PLI-linked revenue.

china_plus_one.evidence: IT services company; no export-manufacturing / supply-chain-diversification narrative applies.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Forward contracts outstanding of approximately USD 300 million as of March 31, 2025.
inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue mix disclosed as North America 80.5%, Europe 8.4%, India 9.3%, Rest of World 1.8%. Persistent held forward contracts of ~USD 300 million outstanding at FY25-end; brokers (Kotak) noted the company's margins are sensitive to INR moves since offshore delivery margins are ~3x onsite margins (roughly 30bps margin impact per 1% INR appreciation), implying only partial hedge coverage relative to total USD billings.

pli_scheme.evidence: Not applicable - IT/software services company, no manufacturing PLI relevance found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Broker/rating-agency notes (HDFC Securities, CARE Ratings) describe NFIL as 'capitalizing on the China plus one supply chain diversification trend,' with 'rising preference for Indian fluorochemical suppliers amid China+1 sentiment' benefiting its export-led Specialty Chemicals/CDMO business (Specialty Chemicals + CDMO were ~51% of total exports in H1FY26, anchored by Bayer Crop Science, Corteva and Fermion). This framing came from third-party analyst reports, not confirmed as verbatim company AR language, hence not rated 'strong.'

crude_exposure.evidence: Key imported raw material is fluorspar (China controls a large share of global supply); NFIL has long-term supply contracts with South African miners and a 25% JV in a domestic fluorspar beneficiation venture to de-risk supply. Energy-intensive processes also expose margins to energy/feedstock costs, but no explicit crude-oil-linked raw-material percentage was disclosed in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company faces two-way forex exposure from significant export revenue (Q4FY25 export contribution cited at ~77%, quarterly not full-year) and imported raw materials (fluorspar); no specific USD revenue % or hedging policy was quantified in sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Engineering consultancy servicing PSU oil & gas capex, not an export-manufacturing business; overseas growth is Middle East/Africa-focused hydrocarbon consultancy expansion (new Saudi Arabia office alongside Abu Dhabi operations), not a supply-chain-diversification-from-China narrative.

govt_capex.evidence: EIL is a Government of India Navratna PSU consultancy whose core clients are PSU oil & gas majors (IOCL, BPCL, HPCL, ONGC, CPCL) - e.g. leading the Visakh Refinery Modernisation Project (VRMP) for HPCL and the P-25 Project for IOCL Panipat. FY25 order book hit an all-time high of Rs 11,700 crore (order inflow Rs 8,214 crore vs Rs 3,400 crore in FY24); oil & gas is still ~55% of the order book with the remaining ~45% in infrastructure, chemicals, fertilisers, power and mining/metallurgy - sectors that are also largely government/PSU capex-driven in India. No single revenue percentage was explicitly tied to 'government capex' in sources reviewed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: No specific floating-rate liability disclosure found; EIL is a consultancy-heavy, asset-light PSU historically carrying low debt levels.

crude_exposure.evidence: EIL is an engineering consultancy/EPC contractor, not a raw-material processor, so direct crude-oil raw-material cost exposure does not apply. Exposure is indirect, via PSU clients' (IOCL/BPCL/HPCL) capex cycles, which can be deferred or accelerated with oil price swings and affect EIL's order inflow and project economics.

inr_exposure.evidence: International operations revenue rose 32% YoY to Rs 371 crore in FY25 against total consolidated revenue of Rs 3,878 crore (~9.6% of revenue, used for the export_pct figure above), driven by growing Middle East/Abu Dhabi consultancy work and a planned Saudi Arabia office. No specific USD revenue % or hedging policy was disclosed in sources reviewed.

rural.evidence: Tractor business growth attributed to 'strong rural sentiment, GST norms and ongoing state subsidies'; two-wheeler market growth (targeted ~8% next quarter) attributed to 'robust rural demand and upcoming festive spending' per company commentary on FY2024-25/FY2025-26 results. No revenue percentage disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Powertrain Solutions segment growth (5.8% in FY24-25) was 'largely driven by the tractor segment and export performance,' indicating a meaningful but undisclosed export component; overall export/domestic revenue split not found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Bosch secured PLI approval on 15 March 2022 under the Component Champion Incentive Scheme (part of the Rs 25,938 crore PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Components), one of 67 companies approved in the Component Champion category. Revenue impact/quantum not disclosed in sources reviewed.

rural.evidence: Tier-III-and-beyond cities contributed approximately 3% of Dr Lal PathLabs' FY2024-25 revenue, growing at a 4-year revenue CAGR of ~17% versus ~14% company-wide, driven by 18 new labs added during the year focused on Tier-3/Tier-4 markets. (Proxy for rural/semi-urban penetration, not a literal 'rural' disclosure.)

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company carries very low leverage: total debt of roughly Rs 1.6 billion against equity of roughly Rs 22.1 billion (debt-to-equity ~7.1%, down from ~12.3% five years prior); specific floating-vs-fixed rate split not disclosed in sources reviewed.

Finance costs fell 26.9% YoY in FY2023-24 and interest coverage ratio improved to 25.4x (from 13.3x in FY2022-23), indicating a reduced and well-covered debt load; exact floating-rate liability percentage not disclosed in sources reviewed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Extra Neutral Alcohol (ENA, sourced from sugarcane molasses and grains) makes up roughly 40% of raw material cost; packaging materials (glass bottles, PET closures), which carry oil-linked cost exposure, are also cited as a key input alongside ENA. Management noted 'inflationary headwinds in key commodities' as an ongoing margin pressure. No raw-material percentage tied specifically to crude oil was disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Sona Comstar's FY2024-25/FY2025-26 disclosures describe supply-chain de-risking rather than a classic 'China+1' revenue-growth framing: (1) plans to localize rare-earth magnet production domestically in direct response to China's April 2025 export restrictions (China supplies ~90% of global rare-earth magnets and Sona is India's largest importer of them); (2) company describes itself as building a 'geographically diversified, vertically integrated presence' across North America, Europe and China's EV markets via 12 manufacturing/assembly facilities in India, USA, Mexico and China, with over 50% of sales international. No explicit AR statement attributes specific revenue/order growth to 'China+1' diversification.

inr_exposure.evidence: North America and Europe together represented roughly 54-66% of revenue across recent quarters (e.g. India 41% / North America 30% / Europe 24% in a Q2 FY2025-26 investor-presentation recap), implying substantial USD/EUR revenue exposure; exact USD-denominated revenue percentage and hedging policy not found in sources reviewed. Figures cited are from a quarterly investor presentation, not confirmed as the FY2024-25 annual report's own disclosure.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sona Comstar received certification under the Auto PLI (Production Linked Incentive) scheme for a hub wheel drive motor for electric two-wheelers, and has filed seven applications for different products under the scheme. Revenue quantum from PLI not disclosed in sources reviewed. (Note: company is not a claimant under the separate ACC Battery PLI scheme.)

govt_capex.evidence: Government of India has been aggregating PSU cargo demand (crude oil imports for IOCL/HPCL/BPCL refineries) to secure long-term charters for Indian carriers including SCI; SCI signed an MoU (Sep 2025) with IOCL/HPCL/BPCL to jointly own/operate crude-import vessels. SCI's tankers carry ~35 MMT/annum of POL cargo. Specific % of SCI revenue tied to government/PSU charters was not disclosed in accessible sources.

crude_exposure.evidence: Bunker fuel is SCI's largest variable operating cost (industry-wide bunker costs typically run 50-60% of shipping opex, and are directly linked to crude oil prices). SCI's board approved partial bunker fuel hedging (forward/swap contracts, price locks of up to 3 years) to manage this exposure. Exact bunker cost as a % of SCI's total opex/raw material cost was not found in accessible sources (Screener and shipindia.com/shipmin.gov.in PDFs were unreachable in this session).

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Uses foreign currency derivatives (forward contracts) designated as cash-flow hedges for freight/charter earnings, in addition to bunker fuel hedges; specific USD revenue % and formal hedging ratio not confirmed.
inr_exposure.evidence: SCI's freight/charter revenue is predominantly USD-denominated per standard shipping industry practice; company faces FX exposure from rupee depreciation on USD debt service. Exact % of revenue in USD not disclosed in accessible sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: Third-party analysis (not confirmed against primary AR text in this session) indicates Zydus is reducing Chinese API sourcing dependency (cited as moving from ~46% toward a ~35% target) to mitigate raw-material/API supply-chain risk. Company also received its first NMPA approval (Venlafaxine ER) to enter the China formulations market itself. This is supply-side/market-entry diversification, not an explicit AR-stated 'China+1 export-growth' narrative.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY2024-25 segment mix: North America (US) Formulations was the largest segment at 44-45% of consolidated revenue (₹1,16,820mn, vs ₹1,10,500mn prior year), India Formulations 25-26%, International Formulations (Europe/emerging markets combined) 13%, Consumer Wellness 11%, Medtech 3%, APIs 2%, Alliances 0.2%. US segment is presumed largely USD-denominated. Formal treasury/hedging policy percentage could not be confirmed from a primary source in this session.

pli_scheme.evidence: India's PLI scheme for Bulk Drugs/APIs/KSMs has approved 48 projects sector-wide (₹6,940 cr outlay); no source found confirming Zydus Lifesciences itself is a named beneficiary or discloses PLI-linked revenue.

china_plus_one.evidence: Reported (Reuters, via Autoguideindia) that Uno Minda and Mahindra are exploring domestic rare-earth magnet manufacturing amid China's export curbs on magnets - a supply-chain risk-mitigation move, not an AR-stated 'China+1 customer diversification drives our export growth' narrative. Separately, exports are growing (Q1 FY27 exports ₹228cr vs ₹141cr in Q4 FY26, +60% QoQ) with new global-OEM wins, but no explicit China+1 framing found for the export/customer side.

inr_exposure.evidence: India accounts for >80% (search-sourced figure) of sales; International Business contributed ~9% of total revenue in a recent quarter (Q1 FY26-27), with exports concentrated in Africa, Latin America and Middle East (not purely USD markets). FY2023-24 full-year consolidated revenue was ₹14,065cr (+24.6% YoY); FY2024-25 (FY25) consolidated revenue ~₹16,700cr (+20% YoY). Formal FX hedging policy could not be confirmed from a primary source in this session.

pli_scheme.evidence: Uno Minda is named among auto-component makers expected to start receiving Auto PLI (component champion) incentives from FY27 onward; as of Dec 2025 nearly all (~99.9%) of scheme payouts had gone to five vehicle (OEM) manufacturers, not component makers like Uno Minda. No confirmed PLI revenue booked by Uno Minda in FY2023-24/FY2024-25 sources found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company/press materials emphasize 'Make in India' server manufacturing (new ₹35cr Faridabad SMT/PCB facility, May 2024), positioning itself as India's only full-stack domestic high-end computing systems provider, recognized by MeitY and partners (Intel, AMD, NVIDIA) for indigenous manufacturing/import substitution. Framed primarily as import-substitution/domestic self-reliance rather than explicit 'China+1' export-customer-diversification language; exports remain small (~5% of revenue) so the narrative is domestic-substitution-led, not export-China+1-led.

govt_capex.evidence: Government plus PSU customers together account for approximately 58% of Netweb's revenue (per investor presentation/press coverage), consistent with its position as a major supplier of HPC/AI/data-center systems to government and public-sector institutions. Top 10 customers contributed 76.4% of FY26 revenue (top 5: 62.2%), reflecting concentration typical of large government/enterprise orders.

inr_exposure.evidence: Management has stated exports are 'not a major growth driver yet' and are expected to remain around 5% of revenue, with domestic AI/HPC demand the primary focus. Netweb's FX exposure is arguably more on the import/procurement side (chips and components sourced from Intel, AMD, NVIDIA) than on export revenue. Formal hedging policy not confirmed from a primary source in this session.

pli_scheme.evidence: Netweb Technologies received a Production Linked Incentive of Rs 5,93,97,758 (~Rs 5.94 crore) under the MeitY PLI Scheme 2.0 for IT Hardware, for the period July 1, 2023 to March 31, 2024 (incentive claim announced/received April 2025). Exact incentive as a % of revenue not disclosed.
